title: 2007 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 7
statement: Forty two cards are labeled with the natural numbers 1 through 42 and randomly shuffled into a stack. One by one, cards are taken off of the top of the stack until a card labeled with a prime number is removed. How many cards are removed on average?

solutions.text: \(\frac{\mathbf{4 3}}{\mathbf{1 4}}\). Note that there are 13 prime numbers amongst the cards. We may view these as separating the remaining 29 cards into 14 groups of nonprimes - those appearing before the first prime, between the first and second, etc. Each of these groups is equally likely to appear first, so 29/14 nonprimes are removed on average. We are done since exactly one prime is always drawn.
